column2: the foolish who approach women not to be approached, those who steal others' property, those who misappropriate deposits, and those who give poison or fire,
those who steal another's land, house, bed, clothing and ornaments, those who are cruel in others' weaknesses, those who always speak falsely,
those who cause great suffering in villages, kingdoms and cities, those who give false witness, sellers of maidens,
those fond of eating forbidden food, those who go to a daughter or daughter-in-law, and those who speak of manliness (boast) to mother and father,
and others who are indicated as doers of great sins — all these enter by the southern gate.
They are not able to enter or go out, the wretched, greatly; the sinners, struck by their own actions, cry out terribly.
There, after being pressed very hard at the entrance by Yama's servants, the sinners are led to where Yama himself stays.
Yama, the god, righteous-souled, doer of dharma, restrainer of all, — thus by a very painful road men arrive at the city of ghosts.
Informed then by the messengers, they are placed before Yama; then those evildoers see him, terrifying,
their eyes struck by sin, their intellect perverted, his mouth terrible with fangs, his glance crooked with frowns,
with raised hair, great beard, quivering lips, eighteen-armed, angry, resembling a heap of dark collyrium,
with raised arms bearing all weapons, joined with a fierce rod, mounted on a great buffalo, with eyes like blazing fire,
wearing red garlands and garments, lofty like a great cloud, with the roar of the dissolution's clouds, as if drinking the great ocean,
as if swallowing the three worlds, as if vomiting fire; and Death standing near him, with the brilliance of the fire of time,
Kritanta, terrible, like the fire of dissolution; Marichi, fierce, Mahamari, and the dreadful Kalaratri,
many painful diseases of many forms, bringing fear, bearing shaktis, spears and goads, nooses, discuses and swords,
bearing thunderbolt-rods, terrible, with razors, quivers and bows, innumerable, very mighty, cruel, dark like collyrium,
Yama's messengers, terrible, with raised hands bearing all weapons. Surrounded by this very terrible retinue,
the most sinful see Yama and the fearsome Chitragupta. Yama rebukes those evildoers greatly.
Chitragupta, the revered one, awakening them with words of dharma:

Ho, doers of evil deeds, stealers of others' property, proud of beauty and strength, violators of others' wives,
brahmapuran:215:58	whatever action one does oneself one himself experiences in turn; so why did you commit evil to destroy yourselves?
brahmapuran:215:59	Why do you grieve now, tormented by your own deeds? Suffer your own sorrows; there is no fault in anyone.

These kings of the earth who have come to me through their own terrible deeds, evil-witted, proud of strength —
brahmapuran:215:61	ho, ho, evil-conducted kings, destroyers of subjects, for the sake of a short-lived kingdom what evil did you do?
brahmapuran:215:62	Out of greed for kingdom and delusion, you punished subjects by force and unjustly; now, kings, enjoy the fruit of that.
brahmapuran:215:63	Where is the kingdom and the wife for whose sake the evil was done? Abandoning all that, you stand alone.
brahmapuran:215:64	We see no force by which you destroyed the people; now, struck by Yama's messengers, what fruit?
Thus reproached with many kinds of words by Yama, the kings, grieving over their own deeds, stay silent.
Having thus declared the deeds of the kings, Dharmaraja himself said these words for the cleansing of their sins:
Ho Chanda, Mahachanda, take these kings and purify them of sins in order in the fires of the hells.
Then quickly rising, seizing the kings by the feet, whirling them with speed, throwing them up and catching them,
Yama's messengers dash them on the stone slab according to each sin's measure, forcefully, as lightning does a great tree.
Then, shattered, he bleeds in streams; the embodied one becomes unconscious and motionless.
Then touched by the wind he slowly revives again; then, for purification of sin, they throw him into the ocean of hells.
Others also, men fond of sinful deeds, greatly pained, the messengers, best of Brahmins, report to Yama:

Lord, by your command this one, greatly bewildered by us, always turned from dharma and devoted to sin, has been brought.
brahmapuran:215:74	This greedy, evil-conducted one, joined with great sins, doer of lesser sins, always fond of harming, impure,
brahmapuran:215:75	approacher of women not to be approached, wicked-souled, robber of others' property, seller of a maiden, false witness, ungrateful, deceiver of friends —
brahmapuran:215:76	by this intoxicated one dharma was always reviled; evil-souled, he did sinful deeds in the world of mortals.
brahmapuran:215:77	Now tell, lord of gods, his punishment and favour; we are in the way of his actions.
Having thus informed the Lord of gods and set the sinner before him, in thousands of hells and in hundreds of millions of hells
the servants then go to seize other men. Yama, when the fault is established of the sinners,
commands those terrible servants of his for punishment, as the punishment of each is indicated by Vasishtha and others.
Yama's servants, greatly angry, carry out that for the sin: with goads, hammers, rods, saws, shaktis and tomaras,
and by falls of swords and spears, the sinners are pierced in thousands of hells and in hundreds of millions of hells.
They are tormented by Yama's servants with the faults acquired by their own deeds. Hear the form of the hells, terrifying,
their names and measure, by which men go to them. The hell famed as Mahavichi is flooded with blood,
mixed with diamond thorns, ten thousand yojanas wide; there, tormented, sunk, he is pierced by diamond thorns.
The killer of a cow, in the very terrible hell, a hundred thousand years; the very terrible Kumbhipaka, a hundred thousand yojanas,
with copper pots, blazing, covered with sand and embers: the slayer of a Brahmin, the seizer of land, the misappropriator of deposits
are burnt there, thrown in, until the dissolution of beings. The Raurava, filled with blazing diamond arrows,
sixty thousand yojanas in length and breadth; there, in the hell, men are pierced by flaming arrows.
Men who give false witness are pressed there like sugarcane. The Manjusha hell is remembered as iron and blazing;
those thrown in are burnt there, who made prisoners. The hell called Apratishtha is of pus, urine and faeces;
the oppressor of a Brahmin falls there head downward. The hell of Vilepaka is terrible, blazing with lac;
the best of Brahmins who drink liquor are submerged and burnt there. The hell called Mahaprabha has high blazing spears;
there those who split husband and wife are pierced by spears. And there is the very terrible hell Jayanti, an iron rock;
by it the sinner who approaches others' wives is crushed. The hell called Shalmala has blazing firm thorns;
by it a woman afflicted by pain, who goes to many men, embraces it. Those who always speak untruth, cutting at others' vital parts,
their tongues are pulled out by Yama's servants, the members of the assembly. Those who look at another's wife with passion and sidelong glances,
their eyes are pierced with arrows by Yama's servants.
Those who go to mother, sister, daughter or daughter-in-law, killers of women, children and the old, as long as fourteen Indras (last), the terrible Mahararurava, full of garlands of flames,
a hell of fourteen thousand yojanas. The man who sets fire to a city, field, house or village
burns there, foolish, as long as the kalpa lasts. The hell famed as Tamisra is a hundred thousand yojanas wide,
terrible with always falling swords, patti-axes and hammers; thieves cast there are beaten by Yama's servants
with spears, shaktis, maces and swords for three hundred kalpas. The one called Mahatamisra is declared twice as large as Tamisra,
full of leeches and snakes, without light, giving great pain. The killer of mother or father and the killer of a trusting friend
remain cut up as long as the earth remains. The hell named Asipattravana gives much pain,
ten thousand yojanas wide, filled with blazing swords; one cast there is struck a hundredfold by those swords;
the killer of a friend is cut up until the dissolution of beings. The hell called Karambhavaluka is ten thousand yojanas,
shaped like a well, surrounded with blazing sand, embers and thorns; one is burnt and pierced for a hundred thousand ten-thousand years three hundred.
By whom people were constantly burnt with terrible false means, the hell Kakola is flooded with worms and pus;
there is cast the evil-souled man who eats sweets alone. The hell Kudmala is full of faeces, urine and blood;
men devoid of the five great sacrifices are cast there. Very foul-smelling, very terrible, crowded with flesh and blood,
the lowest of men who eat forbidden food fall there. A great banyan-like hell crowded with worms and insects, full of corpses —
the man who sells a maiden falls there head downward. The terrible hell named Tilapaka is remembered;
there those fond of causing pain to others are pressed like sesame. The hell Tailapaka has a flood of blazing oil on the ground;
the killer of a friend and the killer of one who has taken refuge is cooked there. The hell named Vajrakapata has diamond chains;
those who made a sale of milk are mercilessly tormented there. The one called Nirucchvasa is dark-blind, free of wind;
one who obstructed the giving of gifts to Brahmins is cast there motionless. The hell Angaropachaya blazes with burning embers;
he is burnt there who did not hand over a gift promised to a Brahmin. The hell called Mahapayi extends a hundred thousand yojanas;
those who always speak untruth are felled there head-down. The hell Mahajvala is fearful with the brightness of flames;
the man who set his mind on sin is burnt there a long time. The hell called Krakacha — men are tormented there
with saws, terrible with diamond edges, who delighted in approaching those not to be approached. The hell Gudapaka is surrounded by pools of blazing jaggery;
the man who caused mixing of varnas is cast and burnt there. The hell called Kshuradhara is covered with sharp razors;
men who seized a Brahmin's land are cut there until the end of the kalpa. The hell called Ambarisha is lit by the fire of dissolution;
the stealer of gold is burnt there for a hundred ten-millions of kalpas. The hell named Vajrakuthara is full of diamonds;
the cutters of trees, sinners, are cut there. The hell called Paritapa is lit by the fire of dissolution;
the poisoner and the stealer of honey, a sinner, is cooked there. The hell Kalasutra is made of diamond thread;
plunderers of others' crops are cut as they wander there. The hell named Kashmala is covered with phlegm and snot;
the man always fond of meat is thrown there for a kalpa. The hell Ugragandha is like saliva, urine and faeces;
those who do not give funeral cakes to ancestors are thrown into that hell. The hell named Durdhara is full of leeches and scorpions;
the eater of bribes stays there ten thousand years. And the hell of great diamond torment is made of diamonds;
those who steal others' wealth, grain or gold are thrown in, burnt and tormented by Yama's servants there.
Those thieves are cut into bits with razors by Yama's messengers. The fools who, having killed a living being, eat it like crows and vultures
are fed their own flesh by Yama's servants until the end of the kalpa. Those who steal others' seat, bed or clothing,
those fools are pierced by Yama's messengers with spears and tomaras. Those evil-minded ones by whom fruit or leaves of men were stolen
are burnt by Yama's angry messengers with straw fires. The man of wicked mind who is always (covetous) of others' property and wife,
a blazing spear is driven into his heart by Yama's messengers. Men who are turned away from dharma by deed, mind or speech
in Yama's world receive terrible torments. Thus in hundreds of thousands and hundreds of ten-millions
of hells they are suffered there by men, sinners. Having done even a little inauspicious action here, a man
gets torment in the terrible hell in the worlds of Yama. Foolish men do not listen to the well-spoken words of dharma;
Who has seen it? they say, arguing with direct perception. Men who with effort commit sin by day and night
do not practise dharma, bewildered even by negligence; those who enjoy fruit only here and turn away from the next world
fall, the lowest of men, into very terrible hells. Living in hell is dreadful, living in heaven gives happiness; men obtain both there, having done good or bad action.
placing their feet on excellent golden jewelled seats, they go in vehicles adorned with hosts of Apsarases.
Men here who plant lovely gardens rich in flowers and fruits, benefactors of men,
go well adorned in the lovely cool shade of trees, served by songs and instruments of excellent women.
Those who give gold or silver, coral or pearl go in vehicles bright with gold.
Givers of land, shining, satisfied with all desires, go in resounding vehicles resembling the risen sun.
Those who give a maiden adorned as Brahma's gift go to Yama's abode in vehicles, surrounded by divine maidens.
Best of Brahmins, those who with supreme devotion give fragrant aloe, camphor and incense of flowers to Brahmins,
fragrant, well dressed, radiant, well adorned, go to Dharma's city in variegated vehicles, adorned.
Givers of lamps go in vehicles lighting the ten directions, shining like fires in vehicles like the sun.
Givers of dwellings go to Dharmaraja's house in houses adorned with gold, resembling the morning sun.
Givers of water vessels and pots and water-jugs go, honoured by Apsarases, proud, on great elephants.
Those who give foot-anointing, head-anointing, and water for bathing and drinking to Brahmins go to Yama's abode on horses.
Those who give rest to Brahmins weary on the road and thin go happily in vehicles drawn by chakravakas.
One who honours a Brahmin with welcome and a seat goes that road happily, supremely satisfied.
One who greets Hari saying "Salutation, god of the Brahmins," and a cow saying "remover of sin," goes happily on that path.
Those who eat at intervals and are free of hypocrisy and falsehood also go that path in vehicles joined with cranes.
Those who live on one meal a day, free of deceit and hypocrisy, go happily to Yama's abode in vehicles drawn by swans.
Those sense-conquering ones who live on one meal every fourth meal-time go to Dharma's city in vehicles drawn by peacocks.
Those of fixed vows who eat on the third day also go to that state in divine vehicles with elephants and chariots.
One who eats on the sixth, pure daily and sense-conquering, goes seated on an elephant, as if Shachi's lord himself.
Dharmaraja's divine city is adorned with many jewels, joined with many sounds, and with cries of victory.
Those who fast a fortnight go in vehicles drawn by tigers to that city of Dharmaraja, served by gods and Asuras.
Those who fast a month with restrained senses also go to Yama's abode in vehicles shining like the sun.
One who with firm vows goes one-pointedly on the great departure goes to Yama's abode in vehicles, served by Gandharvas.
One who disciplines his body with a Vaishnava inner self goes here in a fire-coloured chariot to the abode of the thirty.
One who enters fire, devoted to Narayana, goes to Yama's abode in a vehicle shining like fire.
A mortal who gives up life remembering the eternal Vishnu goes to Dharma's city in a vehicle shining like the sun.
A man who enters water and gives up life goes happily in a vehicle like the orb of the moon.
A Vaishnava who gives his own body to vultures goes to Yama's abode in an excellent golden chariot.
One who meets death in the seizing of women or cows or in battle goes shining like the sun, served by divine maidens.
Vaishnavas who, sense-conquering, make pilgrimages go that terrible path adorned with comfortable vehicles.
Those who sacrifice, best of Brahmins, with sacrifices of ample fees go happily in vehicles like heated gold.
Those who do no harm to others, who maintain servants and the like, go happily in vehicles bright with gold.
Those who are patient toward all beings, who give fearlessness to creatures, free of anger and delusion, free of pride, with restrained senses,
of great radiance, go in vehicles shining like the full moon to the city of Vaivasvata, served by gods and Gandharvas.
Those who with single-mindedness worship Vishnu, Brahma, Tryambaka (Shiva) and the Sun go in vehicles bright as the sun.
Those who do not eat meat, endowed with truth and purity, also go happily to Dharmaraja's city.
There is nothing sweeter than meat among foods to eat; therefore one should not eat meat; there is no rising of happiness through sweets.
One who gives a thousand cows and one who does not eat meat were declared equal in ancient times by Brahma, best of Veda-knowers.
Whatever merit in all holy places, whatever fruit in all sacrifices, Brahmins, in non-eating of meat that is equal to it.
Thus the righteous go happily to Yama's world, devoted to gifts and vows, in vehicles to where the god, the Sun's son, is.
Seeing those righteous ones, the god Yama himself honours them with welcome, seat, foot-water, arghya and pleasant words:

Blessed are you, great-souled ones, doers of your own good, since you have done good for the sake of divine happiness.
brahmapuran:216:70	Mounting this vehicle, adorned with the enjoyments of divine women, go to heaven, incomparable, joined with all desires.
